## Daylight-saving-time artefacts (timestamps are naive local wall-clock time)

- Spring-forward (2023-03-12, 2024-03-10): local hour 02 does not exist, so hour-02 counts are ~0 on those dates and trips spanning the gap look 1 h too long.
- Fall-back (2023-11-05, 2024-11-03): local hour 01 occurs twice and is pooled into one 'hour 1' bin (roughly double); trips that start in the 1st 01:xx and end in the 2nd 01:xx look up to 1 h too short, and some become negative (removed by R3).
- Rows with negative duration overall: 643; zero duration: 0; below -30 min: 548 (see the per-date table below: if all negative rows fall on the two fall-back dates, R3 is a DST artefact, not bad data).

Non-positive durations on DST dates:

| date | nonpositive | lt_neg_30min | rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-03-12 | 0 | 0 | 56572 |
| 2023-11-05 | 324 | 265 | 112478 |
| 2024-03-10 | 0 | 0 | 61785 |
| 2024-11-03 | 319 | 283 | 129235 |

|---|---|

Clean trips by local hour on DST dates (hours 0-4):

| date | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-03-12 | 1046 | 781 | 0 | 616 | 406 |

These affect at most 4 of 731 days and the 1-2 h bins on them; the effect on seasonal/weekly/hourly summaries is negligible, but day-level hourly bootstrap should consider excluding the 4 DST dates for sensitivity.
